subject: how to combine your data into defined intervals with custom names

messages.author: 08f3062efe0fd1ca
messages.subject: how to combine your data into defined intervals with custom names
parts:
Dear list,

I would just like to share a quick function I learned on how to group your observations.

I have a vector of values called "nmv".

[1]  876  876  984  984  976  976 1004 1004  751  751  931  931 1049 1049  963
[16]  963 1071 1071  951  933  933  842  842  969  969 1096 1096 1098 1098 1077
[31] 1077  938  938  951  861  861  815  815  772  772  797  797  814  814  868
[46]  868 1179 1179 1114 1114 1070 1070  996  996  997  997 1136 1136 1046 1046
[61] 1015 1015  896  896

What I would like to do is group values from different intervals into one variable. I would like them to be characters (and not numbers). I used cars package and function recode(). Notice the use of " and '. I haven't tested if it makes any difference to use any other "quotation marks".

recode(nmv, "600:760='A'; 761:930='B'; 931:1200='C'")

And this is how the above vector looks like after being recoded.

[1] "B" "B" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "A" "A" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C"
[20] "C" "C" "B" "B" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "B" "B" "B" "B"
[39] "B" "B" "B" "B" "B" "B" "B" "B" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "C"
[58] "C" "C" "C" "C" "C" "B" "B"

If you have any interesting solutions to your problem, don't hesitate to post them.

Cheers,
Roman

parts:
FWIW, base package function that can do something similar is called cut(). I used it like so:


1> st_zir2
 [1]   0  11  88   0   2   0   0  48  23   0  96 130  56 102  11  26   0   2   3
[20]   2   1   0   0   5   1 165 252   1   0   1   0   5   5   0   0   2   0   0
[39]   0   0  13   5   0   0   8   0   0  10   0   5  61  60  31  23   2   0   0
[58]   0   3   6 370 145   0   0

st_zir_kat <- cut(st_zir2, breaks=c(0,1,50,100,500), labels=c("0", "1-50", "51-100", "101-500"), include.lowest=T)

1> st_zir_kat
 [1] 0       1-50    51-100  0       1-50    0       0       1-50    1-50  
[10] 0       51-100  101-500 51-100  101-500 1-50    1-50    0       1-50  
[19] 1-50    1-50    0       0       0       1-50    0       101-500 101-500
[28] 0       0       0       0       1-50    1-50    0       0       1-50  
[37] 0       0       0       0       1-50    1-50    0       0       1-50  
[46] 0       0       1-50    0       1-50    51-100  51-100  1-50    1-50  
[55] 1-50    0       0       0       1-50    1-50    101-500 101-500 0     
[64] 0     
Levels: 0 1-50 51-100 101-500

Result is a factor (which is kind of expected, if you think about it):

1> is.vector(st_zir2)
[1] TRUE
1> is.factor(st_zir_kat)
[1] TRUE


Cheers,
Roman
